findings.title: Rollover carries overspending forward instead of unspent money
findings.explanation: carry = max(spent - available, ZERO) is the overspend, so with rollover an under-spent month carries nothing and an over-spent month increases next month's budget by the amount overspent. The docstring says unspent money rolls over and overspending is never carried. It must be max(available - spent, ZERO). Verified: limit 100, spent 30 -> next month 100 (expected 170); limit 10, spent 30 -> next month 30 (expected 10).

findings.title: SQL injection in Ledger.search
findings.explanation: The search text is interpolated into the SQL string with an f-string. Any quote breaks the query (search("it's") raises sqlite3.OperationalError) and crafted input can change the WHERE clause (e.g. "' OR 1=1 OR '") to read every transaction. Use a bound parameter: memo LIKE ? with '%' + text + '%', escaping % and _ with an ESCAPE clause so they are matched literally.

findings.title: Transfer is not atomic; money can vanish
findings.explanation: The withdrawal is committed by the first record() call before the deposit is attempted. If the deposit fails (unknown target account, DB error), the source has been debited with no matching credit. Verified: transfer('c', 'nope', ...) raises KeyError after reducing the balance of 'c' by the amount. Both inserts must run in one SQLite transaction, and the target should be validated before anything is written.

findings.title: Overdraft check runs outside the insert transaction (check-then-act race)
findings.explanation: The balance is read and compared in separate statements before the 'with self._conn' block that inserts the transaction. Two writers (threads or processes sharing the database file) can both pass the check and drive a no-overdraft account below zero. The balance read and insert should happen in a single transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE) or be enforced in SQL.

findings.title: No-overdraft account can be opened with a negative balance
findings.explanation: open_account accepts a negative opening balance even when allow_overdraft is False, violating the Account invariant that such accounts never go below zero (verified: opening -50 gives balance -50.00). Reject opening < 0 unless overdraft is allowed.

findings.title: Foreign keys not enforced and connection never closed
findings.explanation: SQLite ignores REFERENCES unless PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is set on the connection, so the schema's account reference is not enforced at the database level. The Ledger also has no close() or context-manager support, so the connection (and file handle/locks for an on-disk database) leaks.

findings.title: Storage layer depends on the presentation layer
findings.explanation: ledger.py imports format_money from budget.report, and report.py imports budgets and summary. The persistence module therefore pulls in the reporting stack just to format an error message, inverting the dependency direction and inviting import cycles. Money formatting belongs in budget.money (or the error should carry the Decimal).

findings.title: Rules due on day 29-31 crash in short months
findings.explanation: date(year, month, rule.day_of_month) raises ValueError('day is out of range for month') for e.g. day_of_month=31 in February/April. The RecurringRule docstring says the rule is then due on the last day of the month. Clamp with min(rule.day_of_month, calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]). This breaks occurrences, post_due and monthly_commitment for any such rule (verified).

findings.title: post_due is not idempotent and partially commits on failure
findings.explanation: Nothing records which occurrences were already posted, so running post_due twice over overlapping ranges posts rent/salary twice. Each record() commits individually, so when one occurrence fails (e.g. InsufficientFundsError) the earlier ones stay in the ledger while the exception propagates, and a retry duplicates them. Track posted (rule, date) pairs or check for existing transactions and post the batch in one transaction.

findings.title: monthly_average divides by number of expenses, not number of months
findings.explanation: The docstring says every calendar month from first's month to last's month counts, including months without spending, but spent is divided by len(expenses). Two expenses of 30 in January over Jan-Mar give 30.00 instead of 20.00 (verified). Divide by len(months_between(month_key(first), month_key(last))).

findings.title: Per-category spending logic duplicated and inconsistent with budgets
findings.explanation: render_month re-implements the per-category totals already in summary.spending_by_category. In addition, summary/report count only expenses (refunds are ignored) while budgets.spent_in_month nets refunds against spending, so the same month's category 'spending' differs between the report and the budget status. One shared definition should be used.

findings.title: Dead helper _right
findings.explanation: _right is never used anywhere in the package; render_month does its own alignment with format specs.

findings.title: Mutable default prerequisites list is shared between courses
findings.explanation: prerequisites defaults to a single [] object, which is stored directly in each Course (line 32). add_prerequisite appends to course.prerequisites (line 41), mutating that shared list, so every course created without explicit prerequisites gains the new prerequisite. Verified: after add_prerequisite('B', 'A'), course C also requires A. The caller's list is also aliased when passed explicitly. Use None as default and copy with list(prerequisites).

findings.title: add_prerequisite allows self-references and cycles
findings.explanation: Nothing prevents add_prerequisite('X', 'X') or A->B->A. Such courses can never be enrolled in, since enrollment requires completing a prerequisite that itself requires them. Reject code == required and detect cycles before appending.

findings.title: Course capacity is not validated
findings.explanation: capacity can be 0 or negative; such a course silently waitlists every student forever. Validate capacity >= 1 (or treat 0 explicitly as closed).

findings.title: Duplicate lesson ids break progress percent
findings.explanation: add_lesson appends without checking for duplicates. percent_complete divides by len(course.lessons) while finished lessons are a set, so a course with a duplicated lesson can never reach 100% even though all_lessons_done (set comparison) says it is finished.

findings.title: Prerequisite check uses any() instead of all()
findings.explanation: A student who completed only one of several prerequisites is allowed to enroll. The docstring and README require every prerequisite. Verified: a course needing P1 and P2 accepts a student who completed only P1. Use all(...).

findings.title: Waitlist promotion is last-in-first-out
findings.explanation: queue.pop() removes the most recently waitlisted student, but the waitlist is documented as first-come-first-served and drop() promises the student who has waited longest. Verified: with b, c, d waiting, dropping a promotes d. Use queue.pop(0) (or a deque.popleft()).

findings.title: Students can re-enroll in a course they already completed
findings.explanation: enroll only refuses students currently seated or waitlisted; a student with the course in _completed can take a seat again, consuming capacity.

findings.title: Completed students keep their seat forever
findings.explanation: Issuing a certificate records completion but leaves the student in the course's enrolled list (eligibility even requires them to stay enrolled). Seats of finished students are never released and waitlisted students are never promoted, so a course fills up permanently after `capacity` completions.

findings.title: Any instructor can override any course's grades
findings.explanation: The docstring says only the instructor who teaches the quiz's course may override a score, but the code only checks actor.role is INSTRUCTOR. An instructor of another course can set any student's score on any quiz, which also makes that student eligible for a certificate. Compare actor.user_id with catalog.course(quiz.course_code).instructor_id.

findings.title: Score overrides cannot lower a grade
findings.explanation: override_score appends the manual result as just another attempt, and best() picks the highest score. A regrade that reduces a score (or corrects a wrongly high one) has no effect on pass/fail, certificates or the transcript. An override should replace or take precedence over graded attempts.

findings.title: Quiz submissions accepted from students not enrolled in the course
findings.explanation: submit grades and stores attempts for any student id without checking that the student is enrolled in the quiz's course, unlike ProgressTracker.complete_lesson which enforces enrollment. Attempts are also unlimited, so answers can be brute-forced while only the best attempt counts.

findings.title: Certificate file names collide between different students/courses
findings.explanation: The name is f'{student_id}-{code}' with every non [A-Za-z0-9_-] character replaced by '_'. Student 'a-b' in course 'c' and student 'a' in course 'b-c' both map to 'a-b-c.txt' (verified), as do ids differing only in '.' vs '_'. One student's certificate silently overwrites another's. Use an unambiguous separator/encoding or a per-student subdirectory, and refuse to overwrite.

findings.title: Pass threshold duplicated instead of using is_passing
findings.explanation: quizzes_passed hard-codes 70 instead of using quizzes.is_passing / PASS_PERCENT, so the certificate rule and the transcript's pass/fail verdict can drift apart if the threshold changes.

findings.title: Quiz and question data are not validated
findings.explanation: Question.answer is not checked against the choices range (an out-of-range answer makes the question unanswerable) and points can be zero or negative. A quiz with no questions has max_score 0, so is_passing (0 >= 0) is always true and the certificate check passes it automatically.

findings.title: Mutable Course objects leak catalog invariants
findings.explanation: Catalog.course()/courses() return the live, mutable Course dataclass, so any caller can change capacity, append unvalidated prerequisites or lessons and bypass the checks in Catalog. Likewise Quiz.questions can be edited after results were recorded, leaving stored QuizResult.max_score inconsistent. Make these value objects immutable (tuples) and route changes through Catalog.

findings.title: Dead function _percent_of_lessons
findings.explanation: _percent_of_lessons is never used and contradicts percent_complete (float with rounding vs integer floor), inviting confusion about which rule is authoritative.

findings.title: Mutable default list shared between FuelLog instances
findings.explanation: `entries: list[FuelEntry] = []` is evaluated once and the list is stored without copying. Every FuelLog() created without arguments shares the same list, so fill-ups added to one log appear in all others (verified: a fresh FuelLog() already contains an entry added to an earlier one). Passing a list also aliases the caller's list, which add() then mutates. Use `entries: list[FuelEntry] | None = None` and `list(entries or [])`.

findings.title: Consumption counts the fuel of the first full-tank fill-up
findings.explanation: The docstring says the liters bought at the first full-tank fill-up were burnt before the measured stretch and must not be counted, but the slice `ordered[first : last + 1]` includes them. Full fill-ups of 40 L at 1000 km and 30 L at 1500 km give 14.0 L/100km instead of 6.0. The slice should be `ordered[first + 1 : last + 1]`.

findings.title: Service due only when BOTH limits passed instead of whichever comes first
findings.explanation: Rules are due by distance or by time, whichever comes first (ServiceRule docstring and README), but is_due returns `km_due and time_due`. A vehicle that drove 50 000 km in a month is never due, and a rule with only one limit set (the other left None, which the class explicitly allows) can never be due at all because the missing limit's flag is always False. Should be `km_due or time_due`.

findings.title: Never-serviced vehicle assumed to have joined the fleet at 0 km
findings.explanation: When there is no service record, the baseline odometer is hard-coded to 0.0. Vehicles that join the fleet with an existing odometer reading (e.g. the 10 000 km Transit in the tests, or any used vehicle) are reported as due by distance even though they have driven nothing since joining. The odometer at in_service_since is not stored anywhere, so the model cannot compute this correctly.

findings.title: Duplicate rule names silently overwrite each other
findings.explanation: Rules are keyed by name in a dict comprehension, so two rules with the same name silently keep only the last one, unlike Fleet.add_vehicle/add_driver which reject duplicate ids. A misconfigured plan loses a rule without any error.

findings.title: Path traversal through the uploaded receipt filename
findings.explanation: Only the suffix of the user-supplied filename is checked; the name itself is joined into the path unchanged. Uploading '../../../evil.pdf' (or an absolute path such as '/etc/x.pdf' or 'C:/x.pdf', which in pathlib replaces the root entirely) makes save_receipt write outside root/receipts/<entry_id>/ (verified: resolves outside the receipts directory), so a driver can create or overwrite arbitrary .pdf/.jpg/.png files. Use Path(filename).name, reject separators, and check that the resolved path stays under the receipts directory.

findings.title: Only vehicles and drivers are persisted; trips, fuel and services are lost
findings.explanation: save_fleet/load_fleet store vehicles and drivers only. TripLog, FuelLog and MaintenancePlan keep their history purely in memory with no save/load path (TripLog restarts ids at 1), yet receipts are written to disk keyed by fuel entry_id. After a restart the receipt folders refer to entries that no longer exist, and new entries reuse the same ids, so new receipts land in (and can overwrite) old entries' folders.

findings.title: Fleet file overwritten in place, not atomically
findings.explanation: write_text truncates the only copy of the fleet data and then writes it; a crash or serialization error part way leaves a corrupt or empty file and the data is lost. Write to a temporary file in the same directory and os.replace it.

findings.title: Cost report ignores retired vehicles' spending in the period
findings.explanation: The report iterates only fleet.active_vehicles(). A vehicle retired after or during the reported period had real fuel and service costs and distance in that period, but it disappears from the report and from the fleet Total line, so reports understate fleet costs and past reports change retroactively when a vehicle is retired.

findings.title: License check duplicates Driver.can_drive
findings.explanation: TripLog.record reimplements the license-validity rule (`day > driver.license_expires`) instead of calling driver.can_drive(day). The rule now lives in two places and can drift apart.

findings.title: Trips can be recorded out of date order; 'oldest first' not guaranteed
findings.explanation: record() never checks that the trip day is not earlier than the vehicle's previous trip, while the odometer logic assumes trips arrive chronologically. A late-entered older trip gets its start_km from a later trip, and trips_for returns insertion order although its docstring promises oldest first. Reject out-of-order days or sort by day.

findings.title: Stored XSS through unescaped display_name
findings.explanation: display_name is free text chosen by the user (User docstring) but is interpolated into the post HTML without html.escape, while the README promises everything users type is escaped. A display name like '<script>...</script>' is rendered verbatim next to every post of that user (verified with Board.render_page).

findings.title: Permanent bans are never active
findings.explanation: is_active returns False whenever until is None, yet Ban and Moderation.ban document a ban without an end date as permanent. Every permanent ban has no effect and the user keeps posting (verified: is_banned is False one hour after a permanent ban). Should be `self.start <= now and (self.until is None or now < self.until)`.

findings.title: Edit window uses timedelta.seconds, ignoring days
findings.explanation: `(now - post.created_at).seconds` is only the seconds component of the timedelta (0..86399), not the total duration. A post created 1 day and 5 minutes ago gives 300 seconds, so its author may edit it again (verified); authors regain edit rights for 15 minutes every 24 hours forever. Use `now - post.created_at < EDIT_WINDOW`.

findings.title: Late-binding lambda sends every mention notification to the last mentioned user
findings.explanation: The lambdas close over the loop variable `user` and run after the loop finishes, so all of them see its last value. A post mentioning @bob and @carl sends two notifications to carl and none to bob (verified). Bind the value at creation (e.g. `lambda user=user: ...` or functools.partial).

findings.title: Any staff member can lift any ban, including their own
findings.explanation: lift_bans only checks actor.is_staff. It applies no role hierarchy (ban requires a higher role than the target) and does not check whether the actor is banned, so a moderator banned by an admin can immediately lift their own ban (verified), and a moderator can undo bans an admin placed.

findings.title: Banned staff can still ban other users
findings.explanation: lock_thread and pin_thread refuse actors who are banned, but ban() never checks is_banned for the actor, so a banned moderator keeps the power to ban members. Permission checks are inconsistent across moderator actions.

findings.title: Ban duration not validated
findings.explanation: days=0 or a negative value creates a ban whose `until` is not after `start`, which is never active, yet it is stored and written to the audit log as a ban. days should be required to be positive.

findings.title: Threshold of 0 or less hides every post
findings.explanation: threshold is not validated; with threshold <= 0, `len(reporters) >= threshold` is true for posts nobody reported, so every visible post passed in gets hidden.

findings.title: lock_thread and pin_thread duplicate the permission checks
findings.explanation: The staff, banned and own-thread checks and the audit logging are copy-pasted between the two methods and only partly repeated in ban/lift_bans, which is how the permission rules have already drifted apart. A shared helper that authorises a moderator action would keep them consistent.

findings.title: Circular import between text and posts
findings.explanation: text.py imports forum.posts (Post, EDIT_GRACE) while posts.py imports forum.text (extract_mentions for Post.mentions). It only works because both use `from forum import module` and deferred annotations; importing names directly would break. The data model also depends on the HTML rendering module. Move mention extraction into its own module, or move was_edited next to the edit rules in posts.

findings.title: Overlap check treats the check-out day as occupied
findings.explanation: overlaps() uses inclusive comparisons (<=). A stay ending on day X conflicts with a new stay starting on day X, and vice versa, so back-to-back bookings are refused even though the guest does not sleep there on the check-out night (README and docstring say the room can be sold again that day). Must be self.check_in < check_out and check_in < self.check_out.

findings.title: Mutable default argument for special_requests
findings.explanation: special_requests defaults to a single shared list. Every reservation made without requests gets that same list object, so add_request() on one reservation appends the request to all of them (and to every future default booking).

findings.title: Caller's special_requests list is stored by reference
findings.explanation: The list passed in is stored as-is instead of copied, so later add_request() calls mutate the caller's list (and any reservation sharing it), and the caller mutating its list silently changes the reservation.

findings.title: VAT charged on the room charge only, not on extras
findings.explanation: vat is computed from room_charge instead of subtotal, so extras (minibar, laundry...) are invoiced without VAT, contrary to the docstring 'VAT is charged on the whole subtotal, room and extras alike'. Under-collects tax on every invoice with extras.

findings.title: Path traversal in InvoiceArchive.read
findings.explanation: name comes from the receipt typed in at the front desk and is joined to root without validation. '../../secret.txt' or an absolute path reads any file readable by the process, despite the docstring promising only archived invoices can be read. Resolve the path and check it is inside root (or only accept names from names()).

findings.title: Archive file name built from unvalidated reference
findings.explanation: The file name is derived from reservation.reference, which can come from restored records (ReservationBook.restore does no validation). A reference containing path separators or '..' makes store() write outside the archive directory. store() also silently overwrites an existing archived invoice with the same reference.

findings.title: Circular import between cancellation and reservations
findings.explanation: cancellation imports hotel.reservations while reservations imports hotel.cancellation. It only works because of the 'from hotel import reservations' module form; importing a name directly or changing import order breaks it. The fee policy should take plain values, or Reservation/Status should live in a module that does not depend on the policy.

findings.title: Reservation book imports the policy module that imports it back
findings.explanation: Other side of the import cycle: reservations depends on cancellation, which depends on reservations for Reservation/Status.

findings.title: Special requests containing '|' are corrupted on export/restore
findings.explanation: records() joins requests with '|' (line 176) and _from_record splits on '|' (line 72) with no escaping. A request such as 'late arrival | after 23:00' comes back as two requests; empty items are also dropped. Use a structured encoding such as a JSON list.

findings.title: restore() performs no validation and is not atomic
findings.explanation: Restored records are appended without checking for duplicate references, unknown room numbers, overlapping active bookings or check_out > check_in (a zero-night record later causes division by zero in fee_for and _average_rate). If a record fails midway, earlier records stay loaded, leaving the book partially restored. Duplicate references make get() return the wrong one.

findings.title: Reference number parsed outside the error handling
findings.explanation: int(reservation.reference[1:]) runs after the try block, so a malformed reference (e.g. 'X12A') raises ValueError without the promised log entry, and after the reservation has already been appended to the book.

findings.title: Mutable Reservation objects leak out of the book
findings.explanation: get()/all()/reserve() return the live mutable Reservation dataclasses, so callers can change status, dates or price directly and bypass the availability and cancellation rules enforced by the book.

findings.title: add_room accepts a room whose type differs from the registered type
findings.explanation: Only the type code is checked. A Room built with RoomType('DBL', ..., base_rate=1) is accepted even though the registered DBL type has another rate or capacity; pricing then uses room.room_type and charges the wrong rate. Compare with (or bind to) the catalog's registered RoomType.

findings.title: Rooms can be taken out of service while they have active bookings
findings.explanation: set_in_service(False) does not check for active reservations, leaving confirmed guests booked into a room the rest of the system considers unavailable, with no warning.

findings.title: Deeply nested O(rooms x reservations) occupancy loop
findings.explanation: For every room the whole reservation list is scanned with four levels of nested ifs and the loop does not stop on the first match. Hard to read and quadratic; it also re-implements the night-overlap logic that belongs to Reservation. Index active reservations by room once.

findings.title: Dead and duplicated helper _average_rate
findings.explanation: _average_rate is never used and duplicates the average-night computation in cancellation.fee_for.

findings.title: Frozen dataclass holds mutable lists
findings.explanation: DailySummary is frozen but arrivals/departures are lists, so the 'immutable' summary can still be mutated; use tuples.

findings.title: to_cents rounds half-even, not half-up
findings.explanation: quantize() without a rounding argument uses the context default ROUND_HALF_EVEN, so 2.345 becomes 2.34 instead of 2.35, contradicting the docstring and README. Every payroll amount is affected. Pass rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP.

findings.title: Prorate arguments swapped for salaried new joiners
findings.explanation: prorate(employee.rate, days_in_month, worked) computes salary * days_in_month / worked instead of salary * worked / days_in_month. Someone joining on 16 April with a 3000 salary is paid 6000 instead of 1500; the more days missed, the more they are paid.

findings.title: Department totals are not reset between departments
findings.explanation: When the department changes only headcount is reset (line 46); gross, deductions and net keep accumulating, so every department after the first includes the money of all previous departments, contrary to the docstring.

findings.title: SQL injection in by_department
findings.explanation: The department typed in by HR on the web form is interpolated into the SQL string. A value like x' OR '1'='1 returns every employee and other payloads can read arbitrary data; a quote in a legitimate department name breaks the query. Use a ? parameter.

findings.title: Timesheet period is not checked against the payslip period
findings.explanation: build_payslip only checks the employee id. A March timesheet passed for an April payslip is silently paid as April hours. Check timesheet.year/month equal year/month.

findings.title: Overtime lost for ISO weeks spanning two months
findings.explanation: A timesheet only holds the days of one month, so a week that straddles a month boundary is split in two and each part is compared to 40 hours separately. 30 h at the end of March plus 20 h at the start of April (50 h in one ISO week) produces no overtime at all, violating the 'above 40 hours in an ISO week' rule.

findings.title: Flat health insurance can make net pay negative
findings.explanation: Health insurance of 25.00 is charged whenever gross > 0. An employee whose gross is below the deductions (e.g. one hour worked) gets a negative net, which then goes into the bank transfer file as a negative payment. Cap deductions at gross or carry the shortfall.

findings.title: parse_amount raises InvalidOperation and accepts NaN/Infinity
findings.explanation: Invalid text such as 'abc' raises decimal.InvalidOperation, not ValueError, so callers handling the documented ValueError miss it. 'NaN' parses and returns NaN; 'Infinity' raises from quantize. Commas are stripped anywhere ('1,2,3' -> 123). Validate the format and finiteness.

findings.title: Overtime rule duplicated in the report module
findings.explanation: overtime_by_department re-implements split_overtime with its own WEEKLY_HOURS constant (line 17) instead of reusing timesheets.split_overtime/OVERTIME_THRESHOLD, so the two can drift apart. It also raises KeyError for a timesheet whose employee is not in the list.

findings.title: Payslip rendering duplicated
findings.explanation: _payslip_block is a copy of Payslip.render_text; any change to the payslip layout must be made twice. Reuse render_text.

findings.title: Connection lifetime not managed
findings.explanation: EmployeeStore opens a SQLite connection in __init__ but offers no context-manager support; any exception between creation and close() leaks the connection.

findings.title: Discount code usable one time more than max_uses
findings.explanation: The used-up check is `times_used > max_uses`, so when times_used == max_uses the code is still accepted and times_used becomes max_uses + 1. The docstring says max_uses is the total number of orders that may use the code; the comparison must be `>=`.

findings.title: Discount truncates instead of rounding to the nearest cent, via float math
findings.explanation: `int(price_cents * (100 - percent_off) / 100)` goes through a float and truncates toward zero, while the docstring promises rounding to the nearest cent. E.g. apply_discount(3333, 10) returns 2999 instead of 3000 and apply_discount(2995, 15) returns 2545 instead of 2546, so customers are systematically under-charged by up to a cent per seat. Money in integer cents should use integer arithmetic with explicit rounding (e.g. (price * (100 - pct) + 50) // 100).

findings.title: Ticket codes generated with non-cryptographic random
findings.explanation: Ticket codes are bearer credentials (the gate admits whoever presents a valid code) but are produced with `random.choices`, a Mersenne Twister PRNG whose output can be predicted after observing enough codes. An attacker who buys a few tickets could forge valid codes for other seats. Use `secrets.choice`/`secrets.token_*`. There is also no uniqueness check against already issued codes.

findings.title: Discount use is consumed even when checkout then fails
findings.explanation: `self.discounts.redeem(...)` increments times_used before the tickets are priced. If `tier_for_seat` raises PricingError for a seat whose row no tier covers (or any later step fails), the order is never created but the limited-use code has already been counted, so a failed checkout burns one of the code's uses. Redeem only after all seats have been priced successfully (or validate first and count the use at the end).

findings.title: Checkout accepts empty holds and events that already started
findings.explanation: Nothing prevents a hold with zero seats (SeatMap.hold accepts an empty list), so checkout creates an order with no tickets that still charges the booking fee. Neither hold() nor checkout() checks `now` against `event.starts_at`, so tickets can be sold for an event that is already over, and such tickets are immediately past the refund deadline.

findings.title: hold() does not reject an empty seat list
findings.explanation: With `seats=[]` the missing list is empty and a hold covering no seats is created and returned; checkout of that hold produces an order of zero tickets charged the booking fee. The method should require at least one seat.

findings.title: Order ids derived from dict length and not unique across offices
findings.explanation: `ORD-{len(self.orders) + 1}` assumes orders are never removed (any removal yields a duplicate id that silently overwrites an existing order) and every TicketOffice restarts at ORD-00001, so ids collide as soon as orders of several events are combined, e.g. in export_orders_csv. Ids are also sequential and guessable, which matters because refund_ticket authorises by order id + ticket code only. Use a dedicated counter or a UUID.

findings.title: Circular import between purchase and refunds
findings.explanation: purchase.py imports refunds (line 10, for refund_deadline) and refunds.py imports purchase (for the TicketOffice type). It only works because refunds uses purchase in annotations under `from __future__ import annotations` and Python falls back to the partially initialised module; any module-level use will raise ImportError. The refund policy (refund_deadline) belongs in a module that does not depend on the office, or the TicketOffice type should be imported under TYPE_CHECKING.

findings.title: Refund has no customer authorisation
findings.explanation: refund_ticket takes only order id and ticket code; it never checks that the caller is the order's customer. Order ids are sequential (ORD-00001, ...) and ticket codes are predictable (random module), so anyone who learns or guesses a code can refund someone else's ticket and put the seat back on sale.

findings.title: Cancelling an event puts its seats back on sale
findings.explanation: cancel_event calls `office.seat_map.release_sold` for every refunded ticket but never marks the event or office as cancelled, so all seats become available again and hold()/checkout() will happily sell tickets for the cancelled event. Also the `order.event_id == office.event.event_id` check is redundant (an office only sells one event) and the if/else accumulation can be a dict.get.

findings.title: Revenue uses the tier price instead of what was paid
findings.explanation: The docstring and README say revenue is what customers actually paid after discounts, but the code adds `ticket.base_price_cents`. Every discounted sale is over-reported in the sales report; it must add `ticket.paid_cents`.

findings.title: CSV formula injection through customer names
findings.explanation: The customer string is written verbatim into orders.csv. A customer name starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` is executed as a formula when the export is opened in Excel/LibreOffice (CSV injection). Customer-controlled cells should be escaped (e.g. prefix with a quote) before export.

findings.title: Duplicated CSV export logic
findings.explanation: export_sales_csv and export_orders_csv repeat the same buffer/encode/write/checksum sequence with only header, rows and file name differing. A shared helper taking (name, header, rows) removes the duplication so a fix (atomic write, escaping, directory creation) only has to be made once.

findings.title: Mutable default argument shares the rejected list between Ingestors
findings.explanation: `rejected: list[Rejection] = []` is evaluated once, so every Ingestor created without an explicit list appends to the same list: rejections of one ingestor show up in all others and the list grows for the life of the process. Use `rejected: list[Rejection] | None = None` and create a new list.

findings.title: Upper limit treated as exclusive although documented inclusive
findings.explanation: LIMITS are documented as both inclusive and the message says `[low, high]`, but the check is `low <= value < high`. A reading with humidity 100 %, temperature 60 C, wind 115 m/s or rain 500 mm is rejected. Saturated air (100 % humidity) is common, so valid readings are dropped. Use `low <= value <= high`.

findings.title: Threshold run is never reset when a reading is back within the limit
findings.explanation: When the value is not past the limit the method returns without clearing `self._runs[station_id]`, contrary to the docstring (a reading within the limit ends the run). Non-consecutive readings are therefore counted as one run (e.g. -1, 5, -1 fires a 2-consecutive frost rule), and because the counter only grows, once it passes `consecutive` the rule can never fire again for that station. Reset the run to 0 on a non-passing reading.

findings.title: Frost counted with <= while frost alert uses <
findings.explanation: frost_readings counts `t <= FROST_LIMIT_C` but frost_rule fires only for `value < limit` ("drops below"). A reading of exactly 0.0 C counts as frost in the daily summary but never raises a frost alert; the two definitions of frost must agree.

findings.title: Circular import between aggregate and alerts
findings.explanation: aggregate imports alerts (only for FROST_LIMIT_C) and alerts imports aggregate (for summarize_all in heavy_rain_days). It works only because both use the other module at call time; any module-level use breaks the import. Shared constants such as FROST_LIMIT_C should live in a lower-level module (models/validation or a constants module) so the dependency goes one way.

findings.title: Quadratic daily aggregation
findings.explanation: summarize_all already groups the readings by station and day, but then calls summarize_day for every station-day, which rescans and re-filters the full readings list each time (readings_for_day). Cost is O(readings x station-days), so a year of data from many stations becomes very slow. Group the readings once (station, day) -> list and summarise each group. The `if summary is not None` branch is also dead because every key has readings.

findings.title: Timezone-aware timestamps crash ingest
findings.explanation: ingest parses taken_at with datetime.fromisoformat, which returns an aware datetime when the payload has an offset (e.g. +02:00). check_timestamp then subtracts a naive `now`, raising TypeError ("can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes"). validate is called outside the try block in Ingestor.ingest, so one station payload with an offset raises out of ingest instead of being rejected. Mixed aware/naive readings also crash the sorts in AlertEngine.process and aggregate. Timestamps should be normalised (e.g. to UTC) at ingest.

findings.title: Future-timestamp check is silently skipped by default
findings.explanation: ingest/ingest_batch default `now` to None and validate only runs check_timestamp when now is given, so unless every caller remembers to pass the time, readings stamped arbitrarily far in the future are accepted. The ingestor should default now to the current time (with an injectable clock for tests).

findings.title: Unknown station reported as a malformed payload
findings.explanation: registry.get raises KeyError for an unknown station, which is caught together with real parse errors and recorded as "malformed payload: \"unknown station 's9'\"". The docstring distinguishes unknown stations from malformed payloads; the station lookup should be handled separately so the rejection reason is accurate.

findings.title: No duplicate detection, rain double counted
findings.explanation: A payload re-sent for the same station and taken_at (a common retry after a network failure) is stored again. Since rain_mm is the rain since the previous reading, duplicates are summed into rain_total_mm, inflating daily totals and possibly triggering heavy-rain alerts; temperature mean is skewed too. Reject or replace readings with an already stored (station_id, taken_at).

findings.title: Invalid batches are dropped silently; deeply nested logic
findings.explanation: A batch that is not a dict or has no station_id returns 0 without recording any rejection, so the upload disappears without trace. A `readings` value that is null raises TypeError out of ingest_batch, and a string is iterated character by character. The five levels of nesting make this hard to follow; use early returns/guard clauses and record a Rejection for every refused batch.

findings.title: Path traversal through station_id in export file name
findings.explanation: The output path is built as `folder / f"{station_id}.csv"` without validating station_id. An id such as `../../etc/x` or an absolute path writes outside the export folder, which is synced to a public file share; conversely a crafted path could overwrite arbitrary files. Validate ids against a safe pattern and check that the resolved path stays inside folder. export_daily_csv's `name` parameter has the same problem (line 57).

findings.title: Non-atomic writes into a folder synced to a public share
findings.explanation: Exports are written in place into a folder that the README says is synced to a public file share; the sync can pick up a half-written or truncated CSV. Write to a temporary file in the same folder and os.replace it into place (same for export_daily_csv at lines 58-73).
